module_title: Banking and Financial Awareness: BASEL Norms and NPA Management (Level 3: Advanced)
introduction: At this advanced level, we analyze the complexities of Basel III (Capital Buffers), Provisioning requirements, the IBC (Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code), and the recently established NARCL. This analytical depth is essential for RBI Grade B, IBPS PO Mains, and descriptive/interview rounds.

core_concepts.title: Basel III (2010) Key Provisions
core_concepts.description:
Introduced after the 2008 global financial crisis, it focuses not just on Capital, but also on 'Liquidity'.
- CAR/CRAR (Capital Adequacy Ratio): Basel III mandates 8%, but the RBI mandates a stricter 9% for Indian banks.
- Capital Conservation Buffer (CCB): Banks must maintain an extra buffer of 2.5% on top of CAR (Total 9% + 2.5% = 11.5%) to absorb stress during tough times.
- LCR (Liquidity Coverage Ratio): Banks must hold a stock of High-Quality Liquid Assets (HQLA) sufficient to survive a 30-day stress scenario (Bank Run).

core_concepts.title: Provisioning Norms
core_concepts.description:
Provisioning means setting aside a portion of current profits to cover potential future losses from NPAs.
- Sub-standard Asset (Secured): 15% provision.
- Doubtful Asset (Secured, 1-3 years): 40% provision.
- Loss Asset: 100% provision (the bank must write off the entire amount from its profits).

core_concepts.title: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC, 2016)
core_concepts.description: A consolidated legal framework to tackle massive corporate defaults (e.g., Kingfisher, Nirav Modi cases). It mandates a time-bound resolution process (maximum 330 days) for corporate insolvency, executed through the NCLT (National Company Law Tribunal).

important_entities.name: NARCL (National Asset Reconstruction Company Ltd)
important_entities.significance: Incorporated in 2021, NARCL aims to acquire stressed assets worth about ₹2 Lakh Crore from various commercial banks. It pays 15% of the agreed value in cash and the remaining 85% in 'Security Receipts (SRs)', which are backed by a Sovereign Guarantee from the Government of India.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: The AT1 Bonds (Additional Tier-1) Mega Trap
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Highly relevant due to the YES Bank crisis. AT1 bonds are unsecured, perpetual bonds issued by banks to shore up their core capital base under Basel III. The massive trap: They have NO maturity date, and if the bank's capital falls below a critical threshold, the RBI has the absolute right to write-off these bonds entirely (make their value zero), meaning investors lose all their money.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Basel III rests on these three pillars: Better Capital (quality and quantity), reduced Leverage (borrowing), and adequate Liquidity. This structure is excellent for framing descriptive answers.

exam_strategy_tips: For RBI Grade B and PO Mains, perfectly differentiate between Tier-1 Capital (Core capital like Equity shares and disclosed reserves) and Tier-2 Capital (Supplementary capital like undisclosed reserves and long-term subordinated debt).
Always pay close attention to the phrasing of the question: If it asks 'Minimum CAR as per Basel Norms', the answer is 8%. If it asks 'Minimum CAR as per RBI for Indian Banks', the answer is 9%.
